overview: The Medford City Council and Community Development Board held a joint meeting to review the draft zoning proposal for the Boston Avenue neighborhood corridor. The Council voted to refer the proposed amendments to the Community Development Board for further review and a formal public hearing.

items.title: Presentation on Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor District
items.summary: Consultants from Innis Land Strategy Group presented a proposed zoning framework involving three sub-districts (BA1, BA2, and BA3) with varying height limits and density standards. The presentation detailed allowable uses, dimensional requirements, and a system of public benefit incentives for increased building height.

items.title: Discussion of Definitions and Development Standards
items.summary: Council and Board members discussed the distinction between lodging houses and co-living arrangements, expressing a desire to clarify definitions to protect low-income housing options while ensuring public safety. The discussion also covered parking minimums, the implementation of Transportation Management Association (TMA) memberships for parking reductions, and green space metrics.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: A development consultant proposed adding a specific 'purpose-built student housing' use category to alleviate pressure on the local housing market. Residents expressed concerns regarding the scale of development, the impact of shadows on residential streets, and the need for clear visualizations of the proposed density.

items.title: Tufts Institutional Zone Discussion
items.summary: The bodies discussed the status of the Tufts Institutional Zone, deciding to focus on establishing a framework rather than a final vote before the end of the fiscal year. Members emphasized that the city should lead the drafting process rather than relying on the university to provide the initial regulatory language.

items.title: Referral of Paper 26093
items.summary: Referred the proposed Boston Avenue neighborhood corridor district zoning amendments to the Community Development Board. The bodies confirmed that the official public hearing is scheduled for June 3rd.
